To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the length of the alkyl chain in the bientate adsorbate influences the interfacial structure of the SAMs and that the fluorocarbon chain is not completely perpendicular to the gold surface, but is tilted at an angle of approximately 30°.
the length of the tailgroup of a bidentate spiroalkanediol has a profound impact on the structure of the SAM formed from the adsorbate, which in turn influences its interfacial properties.

the structure of the hydrocarbon tailgroup in the adsorbate influences the packing of the SAMs, and that the fluorinated segments in the adsorbats can be used as a probe of the packing of the monolayers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and characterization of a series of unsymmetri- cal spiroalkanediothiols having fluorinated and hydrocarbon tailgroups of varying length.
the synthesis and characterization of unsymmetrical bidentate spiroalkanedihols having mixed hydrocarbon-fluorocarbon tailgroups of varying length.

the synthesis of a custom-designed series of bidentate spiroalkanedisulfide adsorbates having fluorocarbon and hydrocarbon tailgroups, the formation of the corresponding monolayers on gold surfaces, and the characterization of the films by a combination of ellipsometry, XPS, PM-IRRAS, and contact angle measurements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the length of the tailgroups of the adsorbate has an important influence on the structure and properties of the resulting self-assembled monomolecular films.

the fluorocarbon-hydrcarbon interactions in the bidentates were responsible for the observed structural disorder in these monolayers, and the disorder was manifested in the form of low film thickness, low packing density, and low wetting properties.
the length of the fluorocarbonyl chain is the most important factor that affects the structure and interchain packing of the SAMs derived form the bidentate spiroalkanedihthiols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fluorocarbon-hydorcarbon interactions in the bidentated adsorbates were not favorable, resulting in films of reduced thickness and increased surface energy.
as the length (n) of the alkyl chain in the bispinocampheyl dithiol adsorbates was increased, the film structure and interfacially related properties of the resulting SAMs were improved.
the fluorocarbon chain in the bientate adsorbates disrupts interchain packing and results in loosely packed, less-ordered monolayers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of the adsorbed film can be tuned by varying the length of the alkyl chain in the bidenate adsorbates.
the length of the alkyl chain in the bidenate spiroalkanediothiol can have a significant effect on the structure, morphology, and interfacial wettability of the monolayers.

the structure and intermolecular interactions of SAMs derived from bidentate adsorptives are strongly influenced by the presence of a phase-incompatible fluorinated chain in the tailgroup, and that the length of the alkyl chain in the adsorptives is an important factor in determining the interfacial properties.
